rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Spherical mirrors form images by reflection. A **real image** is where reflected rays truly intersect — it can be thrown on a screen and is inverted; a **virtual image** is where rays only *appear* to meet — erect, behind the mirror, never on a screen.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - m = −v/u (Cartesian); |m| > 1 enlarged, |m| < 1 diminished - Object at F: image at infinity; object at C: m = −1

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Virtual ≠ fake:** a virtual image has a definite position and can be photographed — the rays just don't really meet there.  ·  **Concave mirrors can give both kinds of image; convex mirrors give only virtual, erect, diminished ones.**

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Virtual describes ray geometry, not image brightness.  ·  State the equation’s sign convention when giving image distances.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***NEB 2024 headlight*** — bulb at focus → reflected beam parallel to axis.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Verified PYQs: image at infinity + object positions 2023 3m; concave vs convex 2020 3m; uses 2024 2m; headlight 2024 2m.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Compare real and virtual images by ray convergence and screen projection.  ·  Where is the image for an object between P and F of a concave mirror?

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Object position ladder: beyond C → small; at C → same; inside C → big; at F → infinity; inside F → virtual erect magnified."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Reasoning (2m): A dentist's mirror gives an erect, magnified image. Where must the tooth be relative to the mirror?** — Within the focal length (between pole and focus), where a concave mirror forms a virtual, erect, magnified image.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Answer the 2023-style question with all three positions (F, C, between C and F).

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Object at F of a concave mirror → image at infinity** (reflected rays parallel) — the searchlight principle.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Real image: rays actually meet, can be caught on screen, inverted.  ·  Virtual image: rays appear to meet behind the mirror, erect, not on a screen.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Convex mirrors are chosen for vehicles not because they form "better" images but because their diminished erect images fit a wide field of view into a small mirror.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: A real image → A  ·  A virtual image is where → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Where Images Come From Bring an object up to a spoon and its face appears; move it out and the image flips. Spherical mirrors — concave and convex — build images by redirecting light rays, and where those rays actually (or apparently) meet decides whether the image is real or virtual.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2020, 2023, 2024) ### 2.1 Real vs virtual images - **Real image:** reflected rays **actually intersect**; can be caught on a screen; always **inverted** (for a mirror acting alone). Formed **in front of** a concave mirror.…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To ray optics of plane mirrors (Class X base):** a plane mirror is the limiting case m = +1, always virtual. - **To Topic 69:** the mirror formula turns these qualitative cases into numbers. - **To reversibility of light:** the "focus → parallel beam" property is just the reverse of "parallel rays → focus".

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: "A real image is formed by the actual intersection of reflected rays; a virtual image by their apparent intersection."  ·  Why does a dentist use a small concave mirror rather than a plane mirror?  ·  Can a convex mirror form a real image of a real object?
